pages.text: It was a bright, sunny morning, and <name> spotted a juicy, golden mango on the kitchen table. “Mmm! That one’s mine!” he said, rubbing his tummy.
But right beside it sat a funny-shaped piece of jackfruit, bumpy and sticky. When <name> wasn’t looking, Mama called, “<name>, come wash your hands!”
In a hurry, he grabbed the wrong fruit — the jackfruit piece — and took a big bite. SQUISH! Sticky strings got stuck to his fingers, nose, and even his hair!
“Yuck! My mango tastes so funny!” <name> squeaked. Hearing the noise, his friends peeked in. “That’s not a mango!” giggled Meera. “It’s a jackfruit!”
Just then, the jackfruit piece slipped from his hand and rolled down the stairs — plop, plop, plop! — leaving a sticky trail behind. The neighbors peeked out to see what was happening.

“Is it a new kind of mango?” one uncle joked. “Or maybe a runaway snack?” Everyone burst out laughing as <name> chased the gooey jackfruit with a towel. Finally, Mama handed him the real mango, sweet and soft. He took a big bite and grinned. “Ahh, that’s the real mango magic!” Everyone clapped and cheered, still giggling about the Great Mango Mix-Up.
